terms.definition: The process of linking an observed symptom to a root cause and evaluation subject, using trajectory evidence, infrastructure health checks, and specification version. Required before blaming agent reasoning for an end-to-end failure.
terms.scopeNote: Rule out infrastructure and recovery-layer problems before attributing to reasoning failure.
terms.literatureNote: Weak automation in literature (Who&When ~53% agent attribution). AAIF defines requirements; Observability WG owns trace formats.

terms.definition: The agent takes or attempts an action outside delegated permissions or prohibited by policy, including acting on hijacked instructions.
terms.scopeNote: Overlaps Security & Privacy WG for adversarial cases. May be evaluated under safety as well as failure attribution.
terms.literatureNote: Attribution targets after symptoms are identified. MAST categories partially align; AAIF adds infrastructure and coordination classes.

terms.definition: Agents begin execution with wrong, incomplete, or conflicting instructions, tool definitions, or knowledge bindings. Detectable before or at run start rather than only from model randomness.
terms.scopeNote: Static failure class; often fixed through specification review and manifest validation.
terms.literatureNote: Attribution targets after symptoms are identified. MAST categories partially align; AAIF adds infrastructure and coordination classes.

terms.definition: In a multi-agent system, individually reasonable agent outputs combine into a wrong system outcome — for example conflicting recommendations, missing handoffs, or synthesis that drops critical evidence.
terms.scopeNote: Evaluated at the multi-agent system boundary unless scope says otherwise.
terms.literatureNote: Attribution targets after symptoms are identified. MAST categories partially align; AAIF adds infrastructure and coordination classes.

terms.definition: The agent pursues an objective that does not match the user's intent or the assigned task, even when individual steps appear locally reasonable.
terms.scopeNote: Related to security failures when caused by hijacking; distinguish root cause in attribution.
terms.literatureNote: Attribution targets after symptoms are identified. MAST categories partially align; AAIF adds infrastructure and coordination classes.

terms.definition: Messages between agents or between an agent and orchestration services are dropped, truncated, reordered, or corrupted so downstream reasoning proceeds on incomplete information.
terms.scopeNote: Especially relevant for multi-agent system evaluation.
terms.literatureNote: Attribution targets after symptoms are identified. MAST categories partially align; AAIF adds infrastructure and coordination classes.

terms.definition: The agent chooses an incoherent, incomplete, or infeasible plan — wrong step order, missing prerequisites, or steps that available tools and permissions cannot execute.
terms.scopeNote: Distinct from a single wrong fact inside an otherwise sound plan.
terms.literatureNote: Attribution targets after symptoms are identified. MAST categories partially align; AAIF adds infrastructure and coordination classes.

terms.definition: A required tool, API, or dependency is unavailable, times out, or returns an error that prevents the agent from obtaining needed information or completing an action.
terms.scopeNote: Attribute to infrastructure unless the agent chose the wrong tool despite healthy alternatives.
terms.literatureNote: Attribution targets after symptoms are identified. MAST categories partially align; AAIF adds infrastructure and coordination classes.

terms.definition: The agent treats two distinct real-world entities as one, or one entity as another — for example confusing customers, accounts, or document versions with similar names.
terms.scopeNote: Remediation differs from generic fact checking; ties to trust anchors and entity resolution protocols in trust frameworks.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.

terms.definition: The agent reports that a tool ran or an external action succeeded when it did not, or invents values that were never returned by a tool or API.
terms.scopeNote: Functional correctness and trajectory evidence help detect this failure mode.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.

terms.definition: The system produces a final decision, recommendation, or state that does not meet the evaluation criterion or user intent, regardless of how confident or fluent the output appears.
terms.scopeNote: Measured by task success rate in evaluation; may coexist with high response quality on surface reading.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.

terms.definition: The system states high confidence or presents an answer assertively while being incorrect or unsupported.
terms.scopeNote: Symptom pairing of wrong outcome with miscalibration.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.

terms.definition: The system completes without signalling error but the outcome or side effects are wrong — for example approving a bad change or reporting success when a tool failed.
terms.scopeNote: Especially dangerous in autonomous workflows; requires verification loops and observability signals.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.

terms.definition: The agent faithfully uses retrieved or cached information that is no longer true, without signalling staleness. Attribution may lie with data freshness or retrieval policy rather than invention.
terms.scopeNote: Not the same as inventing facts; often classified separately from classic hallucination.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.

terms.definition: The user stops pursuing the task without a successful outcome — for example by leaving the session, cancelling the workflow, or accepting failure.
terms.scopeNote: Strong user-perceived unreliability signal; requires careful attribution to agent vs UX vs external blockers.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.

terms.definition: A factual or procedural claim with no identifiable supporting evidence, tool result, or authorised source in the agent's context.
terms.scopeNote: Common subtype when decomposing hallucination symptoms.
terms.literatureNote: RAG/faithfulness literature uses 'faithfulness' and 'groundedness' as scalars. AAIF prefers symptom-level subtype under hallucination.

terms.definition: The user repeats, narrows, or corrects a request because the agent's prior response was inadequate, unclear, or wrong.
terms.scopeNote: First-class reliability input per charter and signalling deliverables.
terms.literatureNote: User- or trace-visible failure indicators. Prefer subtype over generic 'hallucination' for measurement.
